sections.content: How many people are "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks"?

265,545 people

were counted on the census as "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks maintain and balance records of financial transactions, oversee the operation of payroll functions and calculate hours worked, wages due and other relevant contributions and deductions.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks", 12.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks" included:

  • delivery drivers and couriers
  • other administrative occupations
  • butchers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks" there were more women than men (74.8% compared with 25.2%).

This means "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 25.2% and women made up 74.8% of "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks" included:

  • probation officers
  • registered mental health nurses
  • professional/chartered company secretaries

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks", 9.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (63.5% compared with 36.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (89.3%) than self-employed (10.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
